title: What News Do People Get on Social Media? Analyzing Exposure and Consumption of News through Data Donations
screen_reason: Browser-extension data-donation panel (CheckMyNews) logging every news post that appeared in the Facebook feeds of 472 U.S. users, Nov 2020-Feb 2021 (143,129 news posts). Section 3.2 reports the share of those exposures coming from sources rated as repeatedly spreading misinformation (5.1%), with source-level ratings from Media Bias Fact Check and NewsGuard. This is behavioural EXPOSURE with an explicit denominator.

estimates.country: U.S. (participants living in the United States, recruited on Prolific across 48 states)
estimates.measure_type: % of the news posts appearing in users' Facebook feeds that came from sources known for repeatedly spreading misinformation
estimates.value_raw: 5.1% (Table 1, 'All news posts' column, 'Misinformation news sources' row)
estimates.denominator: 143,129 news posts received in the Facebook feeds of 472 U.S. data donors between Nov 2020 and Feb 2021 (out of 889,438 total Facebook posts logged)
estimates.definition: A news post counted in the numerator if the Facebook page publishing it, or the domain of its landing URL, was flagged by Media Bias Fact Check or NewsGuard as repeatedly spreading misinformation, fake news or conspiracy theories (456 domains / 467 Facebook pages); post quality is inherited from the source
estimates.misinfo_def: 'Though the two agencies used different terminology to capture the full spectrum of misleading news practices, they always included the terms "Conspiracy," "Fake News," or "Misinformation." Consequently, we flagged a source as spreading misinformation if one of these terms was used to describe it.'
estimates.source_quote: Table 1 represents the fraction of posts from factual, misinformation, and under-the-radar sources across all users. It shows that 5.1% of news posts users are exposed to are from news sources known for repeatedly spreading misinformation.
estimates.page_loc: Section 3.2 'Quality of Social Media News', p. 2375; Table 1
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Source-level ratings from two independent news-ecosystem auditors, Media Bias Fact Check (2,062 sites) and NewsGuard (2,939 sites), aggregated into 4,149 'Established News Sites'; a source flagged as misinformation if described with 'Conspiracy', 'Fake News' or 'Misinformation'; the two providers disagreed on only 33 domains, resolved by applying the misinformation label; 456 sources (11% of the 4,149) so labelled
estimates.moderator_quote: We characterize the quality of a news post at the source level, i.e., we consider a post to have the same quality as the media source publishing the news... Our dataset includes 889,438 Facebook posts received by 472 users; 143,129 (16%) posts are news-related.
estimates.notes: Exposure (what appeared on screen), not consumption: the same paper shows users interacted with only 2.6% (visible) / 2.8% (hidden) of news posts. Denominator is news posts only (not all Facebook posts), hence denom_scope=news_diet; misinformation as a share of ALL logged Facebook posts would be 5.1% x 16%, which was NOT computed (R8). Table 1's caption reads 'The table excludes posts from under-the-radar sources and posts from established sources rated as Mixed', which contradicts the same table carrying an under-the-radar row and the body text ('5.1% of news posts users are exposed to'); the body text reading (denominator = all news posts, with mixed/unrated making up the residual, since 63% + 5.1% + 13% = 81.1%) was adopted. Note the 456 misinformation domains are the only source of the numerator, so unrated/under-the-radar exposure is NOT counted here.

estimates.country: U.S. (participants living in the United States, recruited on Prolific across 48 states)
estimates.measure_type: % of the news posts appearing in users' Facebook feeds that came from 'under-the-radar' news sources (sites claiming to be news outlets but unvetted by Media Bias Fact Check or NewsGuard, treated by the authors as potentially suspicious)
estimates.value_raw: 13% (Table 1, 'All news posts' column, 'Under-the-radar news sources' row)
estimates.denominator: 143,129 news posts received in the Facebook feeds of 472 U.S. data donors between Nov 2020 and Feb 2021
estimates.definition: A news post counted if its source was one of the 8,489 'under-the-radar' domains (10,128 Facebook pages) that claim to be news media on Facebook but are not reviewed by Media Bias Fact Check or NewsGuard; the authors treat these as potentially suspicious ('pink slime'/advocacy-created outlets) but do not verify their content
estimates.misinfo_def: 'While not all under-the-radar sites necessarily spread low-quality information, we know that advocacy groups have created under-the-radar news sources shortly before the U.S. elections to spread information (or misinformation). Hence, we consider them as potentially suspicious.'
estimates.source_quote: On the other hand, 13% of news received by users are from under-the-radar news sources.
estimates.page_loc: Section 3.2 'Quality of Social Media News', pp. 2375-2376; Table 1
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Residual category: sources absent from the Media Bias Fact Check / NewsGuard lists but self-described as 'News Media' on Facebook (gathered from the Facebook Ad Library, June 2018-June 2020, plus page 'About' sections). No veracity assessment of these sources was performed
estimates.moderator_quote: (b) Whether it is an under-the-radar news source not covered by Media Bias Fact Check and News Guard. While not all under-the-radar sites necessarily spread low-quality information... Hence, we consider them as potentially suspicious.
estimates.notes: BORDERLINE / DEFINITION VARIANT of the 5.1% row: the same denominator, a broader (and weaker) numerator. These sources are UNRATED, not rated unreliable - no truth or reliability judgement was made about them - so an adjudicator may reasonably drop this row entirely. Kept because the paper presents it as its second quality indicator and because it bounds how much exposure sits outside the vetted ecosystem (5.1% rated-misinformation vs a further 13% unvetted). breadth='' because the classification is source-level, not a veracity judgement of items.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) The four exposure-mechanism breakdowns of the SAME denominator were deliberately not made into rows, to avoid double-counting the pooled 5.1%: misinformation-source share by mechanism = selective 5.8%, incidental 5.0%, algorithmic 4.5%, targeted 2.5% (chi-squared p < 0.001); factual-source share = all 63%, targeted 52%, selective 64%, incidental 66%, algorithmic 64%; under-the-radar share = all 13%, targeted 32%, selective 16%, algorithmic 12%, incidental 7%. If the review wants channel-level rows, these are verbatim in Table 1 and in the Section 3.2 text. (2) 'Out of the 4,149 domains in the Established News Sites list, 456 (11%) are considered low-quality (i.e., repeatedly spreading misinformation)' - not extracted: this describes the composition of the two auditors' rating databases, not a sampled population of websites, and is an input to the coding rather than an audience-level measure. (3) '143,129 (16%) posts are news-related' out of 889,438 Facebook posts - a news-share, not a misinformation share; misinformation as a share of ALL posts (5.1% x 16%) was NOT computed (R8). (4) Interaction/consumption figures (visible interactions on 2.6% and hidden on 2.8% of news posts; landing URLs accessed for 14% of shared posts; party-by-leaning interaction rates 1.8-4.1%; median visibility 6.7s for misinformation vs 6.0s factual) measure engagement with news, not misinformation prevalence. (5) Diversity figures (83.8% of users exposed to both left and right sources; 28%/22%/17%/13% with balanced diets) are political-diversity, not misinformation. (6) Figure 3's per-quality interaction percentages for misinformation sources are only readable from the figure and are garbled in this text file, so they were not transcribed. (7) No estimate of the share of USERS exposed at least once (REACH) is reported.

rob.design: Data-donation panel with passive browser logging. 889 U.S. Prolific participants agreed to install the CheckMyNews Chrome extension (Nov 2, 2020 - Feb 15, 2021, centred on the U.S. presidential election); 720 installed successfully, 580 logged into Facebook, and 472 met the retention/activity threshold (at least 30 minutes on Facebook or more than ten news posts) and form the analytic sample. The tool logs every news post rendered in the feed, its visibility time and interactions, matched against a compiled list of 12,638 U.S. news domains / 14,451 Facebook pages. Quality labels assigned at source level from Media Bias Fact Check and NewsGuard (456 misinformation domains, 2,942 factual, 723 mixed, 28 unevaluated); inter-provider disagreement on 33 domains resolved toward the misinformation label. Stated limitations: no mobile capture (desktop browser only); self-selection into data donation; panel is 65% male, 54% aged 20-40, 76% self-identified Democrats, 74% White - not representative of U.S. Facebook users. No response rate in the survey sense; attrition documented (889 -> 472).
rob.item6_quote: Though the two agencies used different terminology to capture the full spectrum of misleading news practices, they always included the terms "Conspiracy," "Fake News," or "Misinformation." Consequently, we flagged a source as spreading misinformation if one of these terms was used to describe it.
rob.item10_quote: It shows that 5.1% of news posts users are exposed to are from news sources known for repeatedly spreading misinformation.
